sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: CFO vs. Net Income Conversion: Operating cash flow converted -531% of reported net profit. Profit is running ahead of cash generation, which points to working-capital or accrual quality issues.
Gross Margin Stability: Gross margin varied with a standard deviation of 9.0 percentage points. Margin volatility suggests commodity exposure or weak pricing power.
Operating Margin Stability: Operating margin standard deviation of 16.7 pp indicates cost swings that make forecasting unreliable.
Share Dilution Check: The share count changed +5.2% a year. Dilution transfers value from existing holders to new issuance.
ROE vs. ROCE Quality: Return on capital employed of 1.7% with ROE of -0.2% is close to or below the cost of capital, so growth destroys rather than creates value.
CapEx Intensity Check: Capital expenditure averaged 39.4% of revenue. Capex intensity is unusual for the business model and needs a return check.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 105 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded -0.6% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.
